This chapter defines the three measures, draws the ROC curve, and runs mlr3's resampling, benchmarking and tuning on changepoint tasks. Every run is small, so the page builds quickly.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(mlr3tuning)
```

## Measures

A `PredictionCpt` holds one predicted `log(lambda)` per sequence. To score it, a measure rebuilds each model path up to the `Kmax` recorded in the prediction, picks the model the penalty selects and compares it with the labels. Measures need the task for this: `prediction$score(measure, task = task)`. `resample()` and `benchmark()` pass it automatically.

Each labelled region is either right or wrong. A region has a false positive when the model puts more changes or peaks in it than the label allows, and a false negative when it puts in fewer than the label needs.

`changepoint.label_error` is the share of labelled regions with an error. Sequences have different numbers of labels, so the measure sums errors and labels over all sequences before dividing. For sequence $i$, let $\mathrm{FP}_i$ and $\mathrm{FN}_i$ be its false positives and false negatives, $L_i$ its number of labels and $w_i$ its measure weight, which is 1 by default:

$$\text{label error} = \frac{\sum_i w_i \left(\mathrm{FP}_i + \mathrm{FN}_i\right)}{\sum_i w_i L_i}.$$

`changepoint.label_accuracy` is one minus the label error.

`changepoint.auc` is the area under the ROC curve. Adding the same constant to every predicted `log(lambda)` moves all sequences towards simpler or more complex models. Each shift gives a false positive rate, the false positives over the regions that can have one, and a true positive rate, one minus the false negatives over the regions that can have one. The curve can loop, so the AUC can exceed 1 (Hillman and Hocking, 2023). It is `NA` when no region can have a false positive, or none can have a false negative.

## Data

The examples use two small tasks of twenty sequences each, one with changepoint labels and one with peak labels. Half the sequences of each have a signal and half are flat.

```{r}
set.seed(36)
signal = vector("list", 20L)
label = vector("list", 20L)
for (i in seq_len(20L)) {
  if (i %% 2L == 1L) {
    signal[[i]] = c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9))
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = "1change")
  } else {
    signal[[i]] = rnorm(100, 0)
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  }
}
cpt_task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "changepoints", backend = data.table(signal = signal, label = label),
  target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
)

counts = vector("list", 20L)
peak_label = vector("list", 20L)
for (i in seq_len(20L)) {
  if (i %% 2L == 1L) {
    counts[[i]] = c(rpois(60, 2), rpois(40, 25), rpois(100, 2))
    peak_label[[i]] = data.table(start = c(1, 55), end = c(50, 105), label = c("noPeaks", "peaks"))
  } else {
    counts[[i]] = rpois(200, 2)
    peak_label[[i]] = data.table(start = 10, end = 190, label = "noPeaks")
  }
}
peak_task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "peaks", backend = data.table(counts = counts, label = peak_label),
  target = "label", sequence = "counts", label_type = "peak"
)
```

## Resampling

`resample()` trains on part of the sequences and scores the rest. This runs three-fold cross-validation of the boosted-tree learner on the changepoint task.

```{r}
measures = msrs(c("changepoint.label_error", "changepoint.auc"))
learner = lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft", Kmax = 3L, nrounds = 20L)
set.seed(1)
rr = resample(cpt_task, learner, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L))
rr$score(measures)[, .(iteration, changepoint.label_error, changepoint.auc)]
rr$aggregate(measures)
```

`$score()` gives one row per fold, and `$aggregate()` averages them.

## The ROC curve

`autoplot(type = "roc")` draws the curve the AUC integrates. Here the predictions of the three folds are pooled, and each sequence keeps the penalty predicted by the model that did not see it.

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "ROC curve of the pooled cross-validated predictions on the changepoint task, with a dot at the predicted penalties."}
autoplot(rr$prediction(), task = cpt_task, type = "roc")
```

Without `type`, `autoplot()` draws the segmentation of each sequence, as in [Getting started](getting-started.html#plots).

## Benchmarking

`benchmark()` runs several learners on several tasks with the same folds for every learner.

```{r}
learners = list(
  lrn("changepoint.intregrcv", Kmax = 3L, n.folds = 2L, min.observations = 2L),
  lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft", Kmax = 3L, nrounds = 20L)
)
set.seed(1)
design = benchmark_grid(list(cpt_task, peak_task), learners, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L))
bmr = benchmark(design)
bmr$aggregate(measures)[, .(task_id, learner_id, changepoint.label_error, changepoint.auc)]
```

mlr3benchmark turns the result into a table of aggregated scores for comparing learners across tasks. `as_benchmark_aggr()` drops the `changepoint.` prefix from the learner and measure ids.

```{r}
ba = mlr3benchmark::as_benchmark_aggr(bmr, measures = measures)
ba
ba$rank_data(meas = "label_error")
```

`$rank_data()` ranks the learners within each task, with rank 1 for the lowest label error. With more tasks, `$friedman_test()` and `autoplot(ba)` compare the ranks.

## Tuning Kmax

`Kmax` can be tuned like any other hyperparameter. `auto_tuner()` from mlr3tuning wraps a learner so that each training run picks `Kmax` by an inner resampling. This one scores a grid of 1 to 4 by label error over two inner folds.

```{r}
at = auto_tuner(
  tuner = tnr("grid_search"),
  learner = lrn("changepoint.xgboost.aft", Kmax = to_tune(1L, 4L), nrounds = 20L),
  resampling = rsmp("cv", folds = 2L),
  measure = msr("changepoint.label_error")
)
```

Resampling the tuned learner gives nested cross-validation: each outer fold is scored with a `Kmax` chosen without it.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
rr_tuned = resample(cpt_task, at, rsmp("cv", folds = 3L), store_models = TRUE)
extract_inner_tuning_results(rr_tuned)[, .(iteration, Kmax, changepoint.label_error)]
rr_tuned$aggregate(measures)
```

The odd sequences need two changes, so `Kmax = 1` leaves a false negative on each of them. Each outer prediction records the `Kmax` its tuner chose, and the measures use it.

## Reference

Hillman J, Hocking TD (2023). Optimizing ROC curves with a sort-based surrogate loss for binary classification and changepoint detection. *Journal of Machine Learning Research*, 24(70), 1 to 24.
